title: Rumi on Letting Go: Give Up Your Tricks, Lover
subtitle: Eight Persian Sufi poems with English translation
yt_title: Rumi on Letting Go | 8 Persian Sufi Poems with English Translation
intro: We hold on tightly: to plans, to fears, to the person we think we are.
Rumi spent his life loosening that grip.
Here are eight passages about letting go, and about what catches us when we do.

poems.name: Give Up Your Tricks

lines.fa: حیلت رها کن عاشقا دیوانه شو دیوانه شو
lines.en: Give up your tricks, lover: go mad, go mad.

lines.fa: و اندر دل آتش درآ پروانه شو پروانه شو
lines.en: Step into the heart of the fire: become a moth, become a moth.

lines.fa: هم خویش را بیگانه کن هم خانه را ویرانه کن
lines.en: Make yourself a stranger to yourself, and let your house fall to ruin;

lines.fa: وآنگه بیا با عاشقان هم‌خانه شو هم‌خانه شو
lines.en: then come and share a house with the lovers.

tafsir: The moth flies straight into the candle flame. In Persian poetry it is the image of total love.
Rumi says: stop calculating. Stop protecting yourself so cleverly.
Let the old house of the self fall down.
Only then is there room to live with the lovers.

poems.name: Become the Gift

lines.fa: شکرانه دادی عشق را از تحفه‌ها و مال‌ها
lines.en: You gave love thank-offerings of gifts and riches;

lines.fa: هل مال را خود را بده شکرانه شو شکرانه شو
lines.en: leave the riches, give yourself: become the thank-offering.

tafsir: It is easy to give things.
It is much harder to give ourselves.
Rumi says love does not want our presents. It wants us.
To let go of ourselves is the real gift.

poems.name: Every Event a Teacher

lines.fa: به جای بوسه اگر خود مرا رسد دشنام
lines.en: If instead of a kiss I receive an insult,

lines.fa: خوشم که حادثه کرده‌ست اوستاد مرا
lines.en: I am content, for what happens has become my teacher.

tafsir: We want kisses. Life sometimes gives us insults.
Rumi lets go of the need for things to go his way.
Whatever comes, he says, comes to teach me.
This is not giving up. It is a deeper kind of trust.

poems.name: Heavy Soul, Made Light

lines.fa: این جان گران‌جان سبکی یافت و بپرید
lines.en: This heavy soul grew light and flew away,

lines.fa: کان رطل گران‌سنگ سبکسار مرا یافت
lines.en: for that heavy cup found me, and made me light.

tafsir: Rumi plays with heavy and light.
His soul was heavy, weighed down by itself.
Then a heavy cup of love found him, and suddenly he could fly.
Sometimes what frees us is not less weight, but a greater weight of love.

poems.name: This Time Is Different

lines.fa: تو را سعادت بادا که ما ز دست شدیم
lines.en: May happiness be yours, for we have let go;

lines.fa: ز دست رفتن این بار نیست چون هر بار
lines.en: this time, losing ourselves is not like every other time.

tafsir: To be gone from one's own hands is a Persian way of saying: I lost control.
We have all lost ourselves before, in anger, in fear.
Rumi says this time is different.
This time he let go into love, and he wishes us the same happiness.

poems.name: The Falcon Moon

lines.fa: بر چرخ سحرگاه یکی ماه عیان شد
lines.en: At dawn a moon appeared in the sky;

lines.fa: از چرخ فرود آمد و در ما نگران شد
lines.en: it came down from the sky and looked at me.

lines.fa: چون باز که برباید مرغی به گه صید
lines.en: Like a falcon that snatches a bird in the hunt,

lines.fa: بربود مرا آن مه و بر چرخ دوان شد
lines.en: that moon seized me and ran back across the sky.

tafsir: Rumi does not climb to the moon. The moon comes down and takes him.
Letting go, here, is being caught.
We cannot make the moment of grace happen.
We can only stop struggling when it arrives.

poems.name: Frozen in Yourself

lines.fa: فسرده چند نشینی میان هستی خویش
lines.en: How long will you sit, frozen, inside your own existence?

lines.fa: تنور آتش عشق و زبانه را چه شدست
lines.en: What has happened to the oven of love's fire, and its flame?

tafsir: Some people are not wicked. They are just frozen inside themselves.
Rumi asks gently: how long will you sit like that?
There is an oven of love's fire nearby.
Step out of yourself, and warm your hands.

poems.name: You No Longer Fit

lines.fa: چنین بودی در اشکمگاه دنیا
lines.en: So you were, in the womb of this world:

lines.fa: بگنجیدی ولی اکنون نگنجی
lines.en: once you fitted inside it, but now you no longer fit.

tafsir: A child in the womb fits perfectly, until it does not.
Then it must be born.
Rumi says the soul is like that in this world. It grows until the old space is too small.
Letting go is sometimes simply being born.
